name: Al-Sharif al-Radi
bio: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn was born in Baghdad in 359 AH (970 CE). During his father's lifetime he became naqib, the official who looked after the affairs of the Prophet's descendants. His love poems set in the Hijaz recall encounters along the pilgrimage route, and his Diwan also includes praise poems and elegies. He wrote on figurative language in the Qur'an and hadith and exchanged letters with the secretary Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'. He died in Baghdad in 406 AH (1015 CE).
